summary: The exact candidate coalesces touching abort ranges and fixes the original shared-boundary assertion, and it fixes the previously reported plain A/B/A allocator-state counterexample. Its request-scoped idempotency fingerprint is still unstable because it includes the version counter shared by every view of ReqToTokenPool.req_to_token: an unrelated row write invalidates A's completed record, so retry A frees A's pages again.

tests.what_was_measured: On recorded base 358c163, actual free_kv_row_segments reached allocator._page_disjoint and reproduced the original shared-page assertion at touching position 5.
The exact candidate freed the two unique pages for touching ranges [0,5) and [5,7) without asserting.
Candidate focused regression suite: 55 tests and 41 subtests passed, including touching hybrid-SWA ranges and plain interleaved A/B/A retry.
On cuda:0 backed by AMD ROCm, independent cases passed for three touching pieces plus a disjoint gap, distinct request-local histories, and not memoizing a failed call.
On cuda:0 backed by AMD ROCm, actual shared-tensor views produced page deltas (2,2), not idempotent (2,0), when row B was written between first cleanup and identical retry of row A.

gpu_evidence: Allocator probes executed with device cuda:0 under torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2 on the assigned AMD GPU; the remaining shared-table-version counterexample reproduced there with deltas (2,2).
remaining_counterexamples: Free row A through views of the shared req_to_token tensor, write any unrelated row B, then retry the identical A ranges. Because the candidate fingerprints the shared tensor _version, retry A misses its completed record and inserts A's two physical pages into free_pages again (observed deltas (2,2), expected (2,0)).
remaining_limitations: The prepared environment has one AMD Instinct GPU with ROCm 7.2 rather than eight NVIDIA B300 GPUs (SM103), and Kimi-K3/DSpark weights are unavailable, so the full TP8/DCP8 multi-rank serving abort replay remains unverified.
No native source changed; repository-environment.json reports native=null and wheel=null, so no native rebuild was applicable. Candidate Python imports were confirmed from /job/repo/python.
